hwe_bench.problem_statement:
## Description
The CVA6 Instruction Trace Interface (ITI) logic in `core/cva6_iti/iti.sv` contains an inferred latch in the combinational generation of `valid_o`. When one cycle produces a valid ITI output and a later cycle on the same output bit should not produce any ITI output, `valid_o` can retain its previous asserted value instead of reflecting only the current inputs.

## Expected Behavior
`valid_o` must be fully determined by the current-cycle inputs on every combinational path. If the current cycle does not produce an ITI record for a given output bit, that `valid_o` bit must be `0`, and the logic must not depend on stored state or an inferred latch to preserve a previous value.

## Actual Behavior
Because `valid_o` is not assigned on all combinational paths, static analysis reports an inferred latch. As a result, `valid_o` can remain high after a previous ITI-producing cycle even when the current cycle should not mark any ITI output as valid.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the output-valid generation logic for the CVA6 Instruction Trace Interface in `core/cva6_iti/iti.sv`.

## Trigger Condition
The issue is triggered by a transition from a cycle that generates a valid ITI output to a following cycle in which no ITI output should be generated for the same output bit.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Produce valid_o solely from the current enable_i and slot_valid_i inputs, with no state retention on inactive paths.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: Incomplete combinational assignment inferred a latch, allowing an instruction-trace valid bit to retain a previous cycle's value.

upstream.title: Fix inferred latch in combinational logic (Issue #3105)
